# 1 Samuel Chapter 30 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 167r–168r | **Source Image:** 1SA_030_page_001.jpg, 1SA_030_page_002.jpg, 1SA_030_page_003.jpg

---

**1** When David and his men reached Ziklag on the third day, they found that the Amalekites had raided the Negev and attacked Ziklag. They had burned it to the ground

**2** and carried off the women and everyone else in it, young and old. They hadn't killed anyone but had taken them all as they moved on.

**3** When David and his men arrived at the town and found it destroyed by fire and their wives, sons, and daughters taken captive,

**4** David and his men wept aloud until they had no strength left to weep.

**5** David's two wives had been captured — Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail, the widow of Nabal from Carmel.

**6** David was in serious danger, because his men were so bitter over the loss of their sons and daughters that they talked of stoning him. But David found strength in the LORD his God.

**7** David said to Abiathar the priest, son of Ahimelech, "Bring me the ephod." Abiathar brought it to him,

**8** and David asked the LORD, "Should I pursue this raiding party? Will I catch them?" The LORD answered, "Pursue them. You will certainly overtake them and rescue everyone."

**9** David set out with his six hundred men, and they came to the brook Besor, where some of them stayed behind.

**10** David continued the pursuit with four hundred men, while two hundred who were too exhausted to cross the brook stayed there.

**11** They found an Egyptian in a field and brought him to David. They gave him food to eat and water to drink,

**12** along with a piece of fig cake and two clusters of raisins. When he had eaten, his strength returned — he had not eaten or drunk anything for three days and three nights.

**13** David asked him, "Who do you belong to? Where are you from?" He said, "I'm an Egyptian, the slave of an Amalekite. My master left me behind three days ago because I got sick.

**14** We had raided the Negev of the Cherethites, the territory of Judah, and the Negev of Caleb. And we burned Ziklag."

**15** David asked, "Can you lead me to this raiding party?" He answered, "Swear to me by God that you won't kill me or hand me back to my master, and I'll take you to them."

**16** He led them down, and there were the Amalekites — scattered across the countryside, eating, drinking, and celebrating the enormous plunder they had taken from Philistine and Judean territory.

**17** David attacked them from twilight until the evening of the next day. Not one of them escaped, except four hundred young men who fled on camels.

**18** David recovered everything the Amalekites had taken, including his two wives.

**19** Nothing was missing — young or old, sons or daughters, plunder or anything else they had stolen. David brought it all back.

**20** He also captured all the flocks and herds, and his men drove them ahead of the other livestock, shouting, "This is David's plunder!"

**21** When David reached the two hundred men who had been too exhausted to follow him and had been left at the brook Besor, they came out to meet David and his men. As David approached, he greeted them warmly.

**22** But some troublemakers among the men who had gone with David said, "Since they didn't go with us, we won't share the plunder with them. Each man can take his wife and children and leave."

**23** David replied, "No, my brothers — you must not do this with what the LORD has given us. He protected us and handed the raiders over to us.

**24** Who is going to agree with you on this? The share of the man who stayed with the supplies is to be the same as the share of the man who went into battle. Everyone shares equally."

**25** David made this a binding rule for Israel from that day on, and it is still in effect today.

**26** When David arrived in Ziklag, he sent some of the plunder to the elders of Judah — to his friends — with this message: "Here is a gift for you from the plunder of the LORD's enemies."

**27** He sent gifts to those in Bethel, Ramoth Negev, and Jattir;

**28** to those in Aroer, Siphmoth, and Eshtemoa;

**29** to those in Racal, the Jerahmeelite towns, and the Kenite towns;

**30** to those in Hormah, Bor-ashan, and Athach;

**31** and to those in Hebron — and to all the other places where David and his men had roamed.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

1. **30:4 — "wept until they had no strength left"**: This is one of the rawest emotional moments in the Hebrew Bible. Hardened warriors — men who had survived years on the run — weeping until physical exhaustion. The text doesn't sentimentalize it. It just reports what grief looks like.

2. **30:6 — "found strength in the LORD"**: The pivotal moment. Everything has collapsed: home burned, families captured, his own men threatening to stone him. David does the one thing Saul cannot do — he turns to God. This is the defining difference between the two kings, and the narrator knows it.

3. **30:24-25 — the spoil-sharing law**: David establishes a principle that will outlast his own reign: those who guard the supplies share equally with those who fight. This isn't just generosity — it's legislation. David is already acting as a king who makes law.

4. **30:26-31 — the gift list**: David sends captured plunder to towns throughout Judah — exactly the communities that sheltered him during his fugitive years. This is simultaneously gratitude and campaign strategy. Within a chapter, he will be anointed king of Judah.

— PNEUMA
